content:
The difference between a House Bill of Lading (HBL) and a Master Bill of Lading (MBL) lies in who issues the document and the parties involved:
• Issuer:
	• HBL: Issued by a freight forwarder or a Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) to the actual customer or exporter.
	• MBL: Issued by the actual ocean shipping line or vessel-operating carrier to the freight forwarder or NVOCC.
• Parties Listed:
	• HBL: Shows the real exporter (shipper) and the real importer (consignee).
	• MBL: Shows the freight forwarder as the shipper and the destination forwarder/agent (or the forwarder's counterpart) as the consignee. 

Tracking using MBL data,/ container number 
Shipping lines tracking system. 
Endoresment letter will be required from MBL consignee to HBL consignee..
comment: A practical point is that discrepancies between HBL and MBL details can create delays during customs clearance and cargo release. Clear alignment between forwarders, carriers, and consignees is critical.
